scope: Read the root-provided qualified Web source and existing local screenshot. This file is the sole write; no repository/qualified-source edits, network, build, runtime/UI control or new test execution.

finding1_domPaintOrder.observation: The existing screenshot shows surviving fragments of NPC labels. World sprite overpainting can produce these fragments without damaged glyphs.
finding1_domPaintOrder.sourceMechanism: Positioned viewport-entity-overlay has z-index 32761 and forms one stacking context. Positioned viewport-sprite-overlay has z-index auto; its positioned map/object/actor descendants participate in the surrounding isolated world context with raw depth values in the millions. Body/building pixels can therefore paint above the whole name overlay. Raising a child name/icon z-index cannot escape its parent stacking context.

worldContext.scopeNote: World-local ordering; not a reason to move names above separate game UI or change input handlers.

depthFormula.domStackNote: DOM actor layers paint inside the stack whose root z-index is objectSortZ+5; their internal order does not escape that context.

effectBounds.qualification: Current reviewed producers only, including explicit targeted/fishing branches; not merely ordinary row-column effects.

preserve: existing absolute positions and motion transforms
applicability: DOM name/quest overlay in the reviewed isolated world context
Known bounded body, map, ordinary-effect, targeted-effect and fishing-effect producers
limits: Not proof that every screenshot fragment uses this particular DOM node/asset; no new live computed-style or pixel probe was run.
Future depth constants or new world producers must keep the inequality verified.
Does not change glyph measurement, text wrapping or the separate pre-clipped GDI image.
GPU world-to-DOM composition and UI handoff still need their own screenshot regression.

finding2_fixedGdiBitmap.evidence: Existing 50x15 PNG was viewed read-only and is already horizontally cut. CSS overflow visible/max-width none cannot restore pixels absent from that file.
finding2_fixedGdiBitmap.lookup: visual-layers requests fixed width 50 and height 15 for a one-line name; 54x32 for multiline. findCrystalGdiTextAsset requires exact fixed dimensions when width/height are supplied.

cssDetails.gdiSpan: inline-block; explicit asset output dimensions; overflow:visible
cssDetails.fallbackStrong: 11px font, 12px line height; no explicit horizontal clipping rule in the nameplate selector

crystalEvidence.measurement: MirLabel.GetSize returns TextRenderer.MeasureText and adds 2px per dimension for outline.
crystalEvidence.placement: DrawName centers the measured label at DisplayRectangle.X+(48 or 50-label.Size.Width)/2; 48/50 is the centering anchor, not the text bitmap maximum.
crystalEvidence.latePass: GameScene draws NameView labels after world objects/effects in its name/effect pass.

finding2_fixedGdiBitmap.candidateNotImplemented: Generate genuinely AutoSize NPC name assets and select/center their intrinsic measured width inside the existing anchor, then compare with the Crystal oracle. Do not globally widen the world hit box just to repair the bitmap.
finding2_fixedGdiBitmap.scopeLimit: This fixed English asset can explain only matching GDI names. Localized or unmatched names render strong text; it is not a universal explanation for every NPC in the screenshot.

recommendedVerificationNotRun.proposal: Extend actual depth/CSS assertions to include regular and explicit targeted/fishing producers and require worldMax < nameOverlay < dropOverlay. Existing depth tests assert entity depth, not this parent overlay order.

Render actual CSS with an opaque overlapping DOM actor/building and a complete known label; compare visible label pixels, including multilingual and multiline labels. TextContent and pointer hit tests alone cannot prove unoccluded painting.
Compare AutoSize name output to the original Crystal MirLabel full-string/per-line bitmap. Existing GDI tests preserve old PNG SHA, so they can bless a pre-clipped fixture.
After any future patch, verify names/quest markers, ground drops, UI windows and both DOM/GPU handoff paths retain their intended click/paint ownership.
